edges.notes: systemd is commonly PID 1 on Linux distributions; not exclusive.
Docker Engine historically targeted Linux namespaces/cgroups.
Substitutable as general-purpose OS kernel in many deployment classes; not a technical 'competition' claim about quality.
AOSP devices ship a Linux kernel fork; see `android-aosp` package.
Linux user-space exec path loads ELF binaries; kernel itself is commonly built as ELF-shaped image before packaging.
Kernel build documentation references GNU assembler and linker in standard GNU/Linux build flows.
LLVM=1 / lld-based kernel build paths exist but are not the only documented flow.
Kernel build documentation traditionally centers on GCC as the C compiler.
Userland on GNU/Linux relies on glibc (or another libc) for syscall wrappers and POSIX/C API atop the kernel.
musl-based Linux userlands use musl syscall wrappers and POSIX/C API atop the kernel.
systemd system extensions rely on Linux overlay/mount facilities documented for systemd-sysext merge.
systemd configuration extensions rely on Linux overlay/mount facilities documented for systemd-confext merge.
Android devices ship a Linux-based kernel with Bionic as the native userspace C library.
